question: If I attack and play an ambush unit, Nidalee, Cat Form and my opponent plays nothing and passes focus, do I get another action?
answer:
Yes — you get focus back.

Playing Nidalee is a card play, not a pass. That play starts a non-initial chain; when it closes, focus moves to the next player in turn order (Rule 347.1.b). Your opponent passing focus is not enough on its own — the Showdown only ends when all players pass in sequence with no card played or ability activated (Rules 347.2.a, 348). So focus comes back to you and you may play another legally timed card or activate an ability.

One nuance worth knowing: if the Combat Chain opened from your "when I attack" triggers, then when that initial chain resolves focus stays with you (Rule 346.1). Only after a chain you started closes does focus pass — and it always cycles back once your opponent declines to act.

question: Can I play a card as hidden from the last rites trigger? Such as playing a tornado warrior as hidden from trash?
answer:
No — hiding is a separate action from playing, and the Hidden keyword only lets you Hide a card from your hand or Champion Zone, never from the trash.

Last Rites' trigger instructs you to play a unit from your trash, which is a Limited Play action. Hide is a Discretionary Action, not a subset of Play (Rule 811.1.c.1), and Hidden's permission is specifically "while this card is in your hand or in your Champion Zone on your turn during an Open State" (Rule 811.1.b). The trash isn't one of those zones, so you can't hide Tornado Warrior off Last Rites — same logic as the Rek'Sai ruling on hiding cards from your deck (FAQ #11271).

You can play Tornado Warrior from your trash with Last Rites, but as a normal play: pay its costs and put it into play as a unit, not facedown. Note its "When you play me from face down" clause won't do anything in that case.

question: if my opponent has Brynhir Thundersong and wants to trigger hidden temporal breach to me playing a unit to base, can they do that?
answer:
No, you cannot react to units being played, you can only react to chain items and units immediately resolve after being finalized. Playing a card is not equal to an ability triggering, your opponent wants to play a hidden temporal breach, not trigger it. And then a hidden Temporal Breach can only target a unit at the battlefield where it was hidden — it can't reach a unit at your Base.

Temporal Breach's "banish a unit" looks unrestricted in print, but when played from facedown the Hidden targeting rule forces the target to be chosen from that battlefield, and the "plays it to the same location" clause is just a linked instruction that follows the unit (CR 811.1.d.2, FAQ #12330). So the play from hidden is illegal against a Base unit. If the unit were at the battlefield where the Breach was hidden, it would work.

Worth flagging two things: Brynhir's "opponents can't play cards" only blocks her controller's opponents, so it doesn't stop your opponent from using their own Breach. And if your opponent's Brynhir trigger has already resolved this turn, you couldn't legally play a unit to Base at all — the only way that play happens is if it was already on the chain before her trigger resolved (FAQ #229, #11777).

question: Does Zhonya's Hourglass trigger a dying ready Riven, Broken Blade exhausting her?
answer:
Yes — because Zhonya's Hourglass exhausts her, and a ready unit that gets exhausted has "become exhausted."

Zhonya's isn't a triggered ability; it's a mandatory replacement effect that kills itself instead and performs its instructions — heal, exhaust, recall — as part of replacing the death (Rule 369.1, 373.1.a; FAQ #5836). Since Riven, Broken Blade is ready, the exhaust actually happens (Rule 415.1.b/c), so her "When I become exhausted" condition is met, the ability goes on the chain, and she can choose a mode that hasn't been chosen yet this turn — Buff me, spend a buff to Stun an enemy unit, or spend a buff to ready me. Note she'll be at Base by the time the trigger resolves (the recall is part of the same instruction), and the ready-me/Stun modes require her to already have a buff to spend, so usually the relevant line is "Buff me" now and ready her on a later exhaust.

One caveat: if she were already exhausted when the kill happened, nothing would happen on the exhaust (Rule 415.1.c), so no trigger.

A power-denominated discount like [A] can cover the power portion of Accelerate even though Accelerate's power normally has to match the unit's domain.

question: For the Show Off mechanic, can I use my chosen champion (still in the champion zone, not on board) to get the Show Off benefit?
answer:
Radiance rules aren't published yet. This uses the printed card and current rules only, and it isn't a ruling on the new mechanics.

No — a Chosen Champion still sitting in the Champion Zone can't be used to satisfy Show Off.

Show Off is shorthand for "As you play [this], you may reveal [Object] from your hand and/or pick [Object] from among friendly game objects on the board" (Rule 832.1.c). The Champion Zone is a non-board zone (Rule 108.3), so a champion there is neither a card in your hand nor a game object on the board — it fails both halves of the Show Off requirement. You'd have to play the champion to your Base or a battlefield you control first, then it can be picked for a later Show Off.

One timing note: the choice to Show Off is locked in during finalization (Rule 832.1.c.2), so you can't pick the champion and then play it in reaction to make the pick legal. question: If the unit that I have chosen to copy with Shady Spectacles die, what happen to the unit that Shady Spectacles attached to?
answer:
Yes — nothing happens to it. The equipped unit stays a copy of the unit you chose; the chosen unit dying doesn't detach Shady Spectacles or end the copy.

The printed duration is "for as long as this is attached to it" — the "it" is the equipped unit, so the copy effect lasts only as long as the Spectacles stay attached to that unit. It ends when the Spectacles detach or the equipped unit leaves play (the equipped unit dying kills the attachment, FAQ #12669), not when the copied unit does. There's also no re-choosing: you pick the unit once, as the Spectacles are attached.

So the equipped unit keeps using the chosen unit's copyable (printed) traits — name, type, tags, cost, domain, rules text, printed Might — and keeps everything of its own: buffs, statuses like Temporary or empowered, and any other gear attached to it (Rules 446.2, 479.1.b.1, 479.4).

One caveat the rules don't state outright: if the unit you chose was itself only a copy of something else (another Spectacles, a Mirror Image token, etc.), the copy effect's target is now a card in a new zone and its layer alterations are gone (Rule 124.1), so the traits carried over would be that card's printed ones. That's my interpretation — no official FAQ covers a copy source leaving play.

question: Can you counter the battlefield ability from Amateur Recital with Not So Fast ?
answer:
Yes — Not So Fast can counter Amateur Recital's hold trigger, as long as the ability chooses one of your units.

Amateur Recital is a battlefield with "When you hold here, you may move a unit at a battlefield to its base." That's a triggered ability that goes on the chain, and because it makes the holder select a specific unit to move, that selection counts as choosing it (FAQ 8771). So if your opponent holds Amateur Recital and chooses your unit, it's an enemy ability that chooses a friendly unit — exactly what Not So Fast's Reaction window is for (FAQ 11189).

Nuances: it must choose a unit friendly to you. If the holder moves their own unit, or the ability targets nothing of yours, Not So Fast has no legal target and can't be played. Also note only the ability is countered — Amateur Recital stays on the battlefield, and it can still trigger again the next time they hold it.

No — she will deal 6 damage total, split among enemy units at battlefields, because you cannot play Mask of Foresight as a reaction or during a showdown, although being able to play it during the showdown wouldn't change Akali's might as well, as attack/defend triggers happen the first time a unit gets assigned an attacker in a combat, which has already happened after Akali's move trigger resolved.

Alpha Strike's damage is locked in when it resolves, not when you play it, so it uses her Might at that moment: 4 base + 2 from her own "when I move to a battlefield" trigger = 6 (FAQ #9355, Rule 359.3.f.2). The targets are chosen at finalization and are capped by the damage available then — up to 6 enemy units at battlefields, each getting at least 1 — and those targets stay chosen even if the split changes later (Rule 355.14).

One thing that matters here: she's at a battlefield with enemies, so this is a Combat Showdown, and Combat Cleanup at the end of the combat heals every unit in play (Rule 468.1.a). So any non-lethal damage you split out gets wiped — only units you actually kill stay dead, though you do bank 1 XP per kill off Alpha Strike.

If you're hoping to soften up defenders before combat damage, that doesn't work; Alpha Strike is better used as reach to finish units off, or from a state where no combat cleanup follows. And remember you have to assign at least 1 damage to the targets you chose

question: if i play reckless innovator it activates his abbility?
answer:
No — playing Reckless Innovator does not trigger his "When I become exhausted" ability.

He enters play exhausted (or ready, if you paid the [Accelerate] cost), and being placed onto the board in a state isn't the same as becoming exhausted. "Exhausting" is an action that applies to a permanent already on the board (Rule 415.1), so nothing has transitioned from ready to exhausted when he resolves — the same logic that keeps entering ready from triggering "becomes ready" abilities (Rule 805.6.a).

So the ability fires the first time he actually goes ready → exhausted: a Standard Move, attacking, or being exhausted as a cost. If you paid Accelerate he's ready and can do that on your next Main Phase; if you didn't, he can't even move until he readies in your Awakening Phase (Rule 415.1.b — an already-exhausted unit can't be exhausted again). question: Can I react with a hidden temporal breach to a raging firebrand when you play me trigger to get his discount twice?
answer:
Partly — you can react to the trigger and the replayed Firebrand's own "when you play me" does fire a second time, but you don't automatically get two separate 5-less spells out of it.

Timing works: the trigger is a chain item, so the state is Closed and your hidden Temporal Breach has [Reaction] (it must have been hidden on a previous turn, and Firebrand has to be at the battlefield where you hid it — a hidden Breach can't reach a unit at Base, CR 811.1.d.2). Breach resolves, banishes Firebrand, and its owner replays it as a new object, so a second "next spell you play costs 5 energy less" trigger goes on the chain. Playing the Breach itself costs [0] from hidden and the replayed unit isn't a spell, so neither consumes a discount.

The catch is the two discounts: whichever trigger resolves first applies to the next spell you play at that moment. If you let both resolve before playing anything, they stack onto the same single spell (10 energy off one card, floored at 0), not 5 off two cards — FAQ #12624. To split them you have to play a Reaction-speed spell in the window after the replayed Firebrand's trigger resolves but while the original trigger is still on the chain; that card takes one 5-off, then the second trigger gives the next spell 5 off.

question:
My enemy has a 5 might unit on a battlefield and combat starts, I attack and my enemy makes my unit move back with a spell. Is this a combat win for them?
Similarly, they star cross it, is this a combat win?
Similarly again, I get stunned, I cannot conquer and recall, this is a tie, correct?
answer:
Partly — they win the combat if only your unit leaves, but not if Star-Crossed clears the battlefield entirely; and a stun only makes it a tie if your unit survives the 5 damage.

Moved/returned to hand: Yes, that's a combat win for them. Once your attacker is gone, the Combat Damage step simply doesn't happen (no opposing units), but the combat still resolves in the Resolution Step, and 468.3.a gives the win to the player who is the only one with units there — the defender. So "when you win a combat" abilities trigger. They don't score a Conquer point though, since they already controlled that battlefield.

Star-Crossed: No. Star-Crossed returns a friendly unit and an enemy unit to hand, so their 5-might unit leaves too. With no units at the battlefield, the result is "No Result" (468.3.d — neither player has units present), so nobody wins the combat, and the battlefield actually becomes Uncontrolled (468.5.b). No conquer point, and no combat-win trigger.

Stunned attacker: It depends on your unit's might. The stun means it deals 0 damage while the defender assigns 5 to it — if your unit has 5 or less might it dies in the damage step, leaving them as the only player with units, so they win the combat. If your unit has 6+ might it survives, gets healed and then recalled during Combat Cleanup, and that recall forces "No Result" — a tie, no combat win for either side, and they keep the battlefield.

One consequence worth noting: you are the Attacker, because the first unit to apply Contested to battlefield B was your unit A (moved by your opponent's own Siren's Song), so Jarvan IV enters the combat with the Attacker designation and Assault's +1 [M].

question: How does last carress interact with Elnuk Herd
answer:

The targeting restriction is a separate rule and does not go away: for a permanent played from face down, the play effect's targets must come from options at the battlefield it was played to (811.1.d.3 — that rule's own example is literally a "next unit you play can be played to any battlefield" spell). So if you move Elnuk elsewhere, the +3 [M] is locked to that new battlefield, not where it was hidden. Elnuk itself counts, so you'll always have at least one legal target.

Then "recycle me if I was played from face down" still fires — Elnuk goes to the bottom of your Main Deck after handing out the +3 [M]. The Buff counter Last Caress gave it is wiped when it leaves play (705), so that part is effectively wasted on the Elnuk; the real value is the +3 [M] on another friendly unit and the surprise placement.

question: End turn step
answer:
No — the "end turn step" is not a window you can act in: when the turn player says they're ending their turn, nothing opens a priority window, so you can't play a reaction or activate anything at end of turn (FAQ 6113, 8978).

The Ending Phase is the Ending Step (at end of turn triggers and effects happen) followed by the Expiration Step, which heals all units, expires all "this turn" effects simultaneously, and empties both rune pools (Rule 317.2). Those steps resolve as Tasks with no discretionary actions granted to either player.

The only way to get to act there is if something is actually put on the Chain — a triggered ability firing "at the end of turn," or a legend/card that triggers in that phase — which gives you a Closed State to respond in with Reaction-timed cards. And note you can't squeeze in a Main-Phase-style action right before the turn ends either; off-turn priority only comes from a chain or a showdown.

question: When a unit gains the Attacker designation mid-combat through an effect like Nidalee, Cat Form's Ambush, does Demacian Standard's attack trigger fire again for that newly attacking unit?
answer:
Yes — Demacian Standard's ability is an attack trigger, so it fires again for the new attacker.

Standard reads "When one or more friendly units attack here, give one of them +2 [M] this turn." That's keyed to the Attacker designation, not to combat starting (Rule 383.4.e), so Nidalee ambushing to that battlefield and gaining the Attacker designation during the following Cleanup is a fresh trigger event — you get another +2 [M] to hand out, on top of whatever the Standard already gave earlier in this combat.

What limits it is per-unit, not per-combat: Attack triggers are only checked the first time each unit gains the Attacker designation in a given combat (Rule 383.4.e.2.a). So bouncing Nidalee out and replaying her, or re-designating the same unit, won't re-fire it — but a genuinely new attacker will.

One caveat: this only works if it's a real Combat Showdown. If Nidalee were played to a battlefield with no enemy units, no Attacker designation is ever granted, so nothing triggers.

question: I use Ekko to play Clocktower Guardian with discount. He dies at the end of the turn and I have a time warp on the top of my deck. What happens?
answer:
Yes — the kill and the Deathknell both resolve before your turn actually ends, so you banish the Time Warp, you may play it right then, and you take the extra turn after this one.

The "Kill me at end of turn" from Boy Who Shattered Time happens in the Ending Step (Rule 317.1), which is before the Expiration Step, so your rune pool hasn't emptied yet (317.2.d) — anything still floating in it is usable for the play. Clocktower Guardian's Deathknell then banishes Time Warp and lets you play it as part of that resolution (same as the combat case in FAQ #12960 — no Open State needed), and "play it" isn't restricted to units, so a spell is fine.

The catch is that the discount only ignores the Energy cost, not Power. Time Warp is 10 Energy / 4 Mind power, so you still need 4 Mind power from ready Mind runes or unspent pool. If you can't pay it, the Time Warp just stays in Banishment — the permission is spent with that resolution, so it doesn't sit around to be played later. If you do pay, Time Warp resolves, banishes itself, and the additional turn is inserted right after your current turn (Rule 738), so you take it before the next player's turn.

question: How does focus priority work when playing a Rengar, Trophy Hunter
answer:
It depends on whose focus window you're in when he hits the table — Rengar is a [Reaction] play (his Ambush lets him go to a battlefield with enemy units even if you have none there), so you can only play him when you hold focus in a Showdown Open State or priority on an existing chain (Rule 347.1). Once his chain item closes and the turn returns to Open, focus moves to the next player in turn order (Rule 346), so you can't play him and then immediately start another chain — your opponent gets first crack.

Two things people usually get wrong here. First, nobody can respond to Rengar being played: units finalize and enter play immediately during the Finalize step (Rule 337.2), so there's no reaction window to the play itself — only triggered abilities (a "when you play me," "when a unit enters here," etc.) go on the chain and can be responded to.

Second, playing him doesn't earn you focus or make you the attacker. The player who applied Contested keeps the Attacker designation and the opening focus (Rule 345); Rengar entering a battlefield you don't control makes you the Defender (FAQ #10056), and any Shield/Assault only matter once combat actually begins. If combat has already started, the combat chain opened from triggered abilities, so focus does not pass when that chain empties (Rule 346.1).

question: Zhonya's Hourglass dies as a unit gear, will Zhonya's Hourglass see itself and recall
answer:
No — a Zhonya's Hourglass that's been turned into a unit gear (e.g. via Lady of Clockwork) does not save itself when it dies.

It does "see" its own death: while it's a unit gear it's a friendly unit, so its replacement effect applies to its own death — Rule 370.2's example literally has a gear-unit Hourglass's effect applying to its own death. But the applied effect is "kill this instead," so the Hourglass gets killed, which is the death that was already happening. The "heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it" then has nothing to reach, because the Hourglass is in the trash rather than on the board, and a replacement effect can't be applied twice to the same death (Rule 370.2).

The self-save only works with two copies: the second Hourglass's effect replaces the kill of the first (Rule 370.2), so one survives and the one whose effect is applied last is the one that dies — you pick that order. None of this uses the chain; replacement effects apply on their own.

question: if i play Baron in a controlled battlefield and my legend is riven The Exile. Did Baron creat the Pit AND enters ready?
answer:
Yes — you get both. Baron's "add the Baron Pit if it's not there already, if you do I enter there" and The Exile's "units you play to battlefields you control enter ready" are both replacement effects that apply to the same enter-the-board event, so as the controller of Baron you choose the order they apply (CR 372, CR 369.3).

Order them so the ready one resolves first and then the Pit relocation: the relocation only rewrites where he enters, it doesn't change the state he enters in. Riven's effect keys off where he was played to (a battlefield you control), which is true, so he still enters ready even though he ends up in the Pit.

Note the Pit arrives uncontrolled, so it becomes Contested and you'll go through a Non-Combat Showdown, then Conquer the Pit after it ends (assuming you haven't already scored it that turn). The one way to miss it: playing him somewhere other than a battlefield you control, e.g. to your Base — then The Exile's condition isn't met and he enters exhausted.

question: Can i replay Dancing Grenade when played with Fizz, Trickster after it got recycled?
answer:
No — once Fizz's recycle replaces the trip to the trash, Dancing Grenade is on the bottom of your deck, and its "play this spell again for [A]" permission only works from the trash.

Fizz's "Then recycle it" is a replacement effect that applies whenever the spell would leave the chain, for any reason — it isn't optional and it doesn't leave you a trashed copy (FAQ #10401). So when Dancing Grenade resolves, the card goes straight to the bottom of the deck instead of the trash, and the recast instruction (which the damaged unit's controller gains) has no card to find.

Worth flagging: the controller who gets the recast option is the controller of the unit that took the 2 damage, not necessarily you — but it doesn't matter here, because the card never lands in anyone's trash. Played normally (not via Fizz), the loop works as usual.

question: When i play a dockside Dockside Lock-Up and use the jarvan trigger to move nidalee in - do i initiate a combat showdown to draw with Nidalee, Cat Form
answer:
It depends on whether enemy units are still there after Dockside's own trigger resolves — with a lone enemy unit there, no combat happens and Nidalee doesn't draw.

You never "initiate" a Combat Showdown; it's staged automatically in a Cleanup, and only once the Chain is empty (Rule 462). Both Dockside Lock-Up's play trigger ("banish a unit here") and Jarvan's move trigger fire off the same event and sit on the Chain together, so both resolve before any combat can open — you choose the order (Rule 383.3.d), but that doesn't save it. With one enemy unit there, it gets banished as the Chain resolves, Nidalee then arrives at a battlefield you don't control with no enemy units present, so you get a Non-Combat Showdown and a Conquer — no combat, no "win a combat," no draw.

If a second enemy unit is still there after the banish, Nidalee arrives with defenders present, Combat is staged, she's the Attacker (she applied Contested) and she draws only if she remains after combat — if she trades and dies, no draw (she isn't present to evaluate the win condition).
